take_homes: Agents can be attacked with plain English in the files and tickets they read, so I need to check what our engineers' agents read and who can write to it.
The cheapest mitigation is not opening the door. Every connector I add org-wide is something I have to maintain and defend.
Package the audit as a skill and run it on each agent. The 'I can't tell' rows are where the real work is.

monday.move: Run the agent-audit skill on our two main engineering agents, focusing on what they read (tickets, Confluence, repos) and who can write to it.
monday.who: Me, plus one engineer who owns the agent setup
monday.stop_condition: I have a ranked risk list and a decision on which one door to close.
monday.blocker: I'd rather build the sales-team setup. Nobody owns the audit, so it gets skipped if I don't block time.

misconception.why: The audit found a risk in my own system that I hadn't thought about, so a good agent doesn't guarantee a safe setup. I'm not convinced checking matters for every output, but the risk list showed me where it does.

one_line: The middle part on agent risks and closing doors was worth it, but there's a lot of filler, and I'd have skipped half the slides if the exercise hadn't found real problems.
